tools.name: list_feeds
tools.description: List every live feed in the workspace: source format, schedule, status, channels, item count, and the latest run summary (including audit issue count). Start here to find feed ids. Archived feeds are not listed: they do not run and do not serve, and only a person can restore one, in the app.

tools.name: get_feed
tools.description: Full detail for one feed: configuration, latest complete run summary, and the size of its rule stack. Works on an archived feed too, and says so, so an id from an earlier conversation resolves to an explanation rather than a not-found.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: The feed's rule stack in execution order: names, enabled state, a plain-English summary, and the full JSON definition of each rule.

tools.name: get_audit_findings
tools.description: Audit findings for the latest complete run, grouped by check with severity, counts, sample item ids, and plain-English guidance on why each finding costs money and how to fix it. The audit measures the DELIVERED feed (after rules). Also returns `opportunities`: attributes left empty whose value was

tools.name: get_field_inventory
tools.description: What the merchant's source feed ACTUALLY contained, and what SKULayer did with each field: every field as their platform sends it, how many items carry a value for it, whether it was recognised as a shopping attribute, kept as a custom attribute, or arrived empty on every row, plus per-attribute cov

tools.name: get_merchant_issues
tools.description: Google's OWN verdict on a feed, from its Merchant Center connection (the app's What Google sees panel): per-issue-code cases with severity, affected-item counts, sample ids, Google's description and documentation link, and an honest lifecycle state — open, fix_shipped (a rule shipped, Google has not

tools.name: get_merchant_link
tools.description: Read this workspace's Merchant Center link. status is linked, pending, expired, error, or none (nothing started). accounts lists Merchant Center account ids and the connection each one belongs to. connections lists stored rows, including revoked, and which feeds are attached. When status is pending

tools.name: search_items
tools.description: Search or page through the items of the latest complete run. Returns delivered items (what channels receive) by default, with base (pre-rules) available via view. query matches id, title, brand, and product type, case-insensitive.

tools.name: preview_rule
tools.description: Preview an UNSAVED rule against a sample of the latest run: match/change/exclusion counts, per-field change tallies, danger warnings (required fields emptied, identifiers stripped, heavy exclusion), audit deltas, and example before/after diffs. Nothing is written anywhere. Rule definition format: {"

tools.name: search_taxonomy
tools.description: Search Google's product taxonomy — the set of valid googleProductCategory values. Returns ranked category paths with their numeric ids, plus whether the query itself is already a valid category (full path or id). Use it to find the right category for a product type, to fix unmatched entries from map

tools.name: get_run_status
tools.description: One run's progress and outcome: status (queued/fetching/auditing/transforming/compiling/complete/failed), item counts, audit issue count, timing, and the error message when a run failed. Use after trigger_run to poll to completion.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: The workspace's recent activity: who did what and when, across the app and every agent connection. Each event has an actor (a human user, an agent via a token or sign-in, or the system scheduler), the action (rule created/updated/enabled/disabled/deleted, run triggered, Merchant Center link started/

tools.name: map_categories
tools.description: Propose a googleProductCategory mapping for a feed: groups the latest run's delivered items by distinct productType, matches each onto Google's taxonomy (exact-path and unique-leaf matches first, then candidate-constrained AI when available and useAi is not false), and returns the mapping table WITH

tools.name: create_rule
tools.description: Create a rule on a feed. The definition is validated, the standard preview runs server-side, and the report comes back WITH the created rule: match/change/exclusion counts, per-field tallies, warnings, and audit deltas. Show the human this report; danger-level warnings mean the rule can empty requir

tools.name: set_rule_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable one rule by id. Disabling takes a rule out of the stack from the next run onward; nothing else about it changes. Use list_rules to find rule ids.

tools.name: delete_rule
tools.description: Delete one rule by id. This is permanent; prefer set_rule_enabled with enabled=false when the human might want the rule back. Takes effect on the next run.

tools.name: trigger_run
tools.description: Start a feed run: fetch the source, apply rules, audit the delivered output, and compile channel files. This tool needs a write-scoped connection. The workspace SKU limit, the manual-run cap, and one run at a time per feed also apply. Returns a runId. Poll get_run_status until it completes. An in-fl

tools.name: start_merchant_link
tools.description: Start connecting Google Merchant Center for this workspace. Returns a short-lived, single-use SKULayer URL the workspace owner must open while signed in as the same person. That page sends them to Google consent and, when Google shows one account, links it. You never receive Google tokens. Optional

tools.name: select_merchant_account
tools.description: Choose which Merchant Center account a feed uses. Required when get_merchant_link lists more than one account. Pass connectionId and accountId from that result, plus feedId. The account must be one Google actually showed for this connection. Owner only. Does not write a feed or a data source to Goog

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "preview_rule" is 1838 chars, far longer than this server's median (363). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_feeds, get_feed, list_rules, get_audit_findings, get_field_inventory, get_merchant_issues, get_merchant_link, get_run_status, get_activity, trigger_run, start_merchant_link · Private data: get_merchant_link, get_activity, trigger_run, start_merchant_link · Public sink: get_audit_findings, get_field_inventory · Destructive: list_feeds, get_feed, get_audit_findings, search_items, preview_rule, get_run_status, get_activity, map_categories, create_rule, set_rule_enabled, delete_rule, trigger_run.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
